The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput under varying sequence lengths. To establish a valid benchmark, the hardware must maintain high memory bandwidth to prevent the benchmark from becoming compute-bound. During the decode benchmark, the primary bottleneck is the KV cache retrieval speed, which dictates the benchmark results. A consistent benchmark requires fixed batch sizes to ensure the benchmark measures pure decoding latency rather than scheduling overhead. 

In this benchmark, token-per-second metrics serve as the primary benchmark indicator. As the benchmark progresses, the benchmark must account for memory fragmentation within the KV cache. If the benchmark utilizes FP16 precision, the benchmark will show higher throughput than if the benchmark employs INT8 quantization. Ultimately, the Gemma B70 decode benchmark provides a standardized benchmark for comparing inference engine efficiency across different GPU architectures. Every benchmark iteration must be reproducible to ensure the benchmark remains a reliable benchmark for scaling laws.
